the ONLY routine that programs the hardware: 6845 CRTC ($FE00/$FE01), Video ULA palette ($FE21), System VIA T1/ACR/IFR/IER, User VIA T1/ACR/IER. 54 instructions, one caller. This is the platform boundary.

the 50 Hz game body, claimed via IRQ1V. Driven by a USER VIA T1 timeout (LDA $FE6D / AND #$40), NOT System VIA vsync. Dispatches on irq_band_state and rewrites the ULA mode + palette per raster band. Chains to saved_irq1v when the interrupt is not its own.
restores saved_irq1v and disables the User VIA interrupt ($FE6E)
the previous IRQ1V, saved so irq1v_handler can chain on via JMP ($4F1D)
raster-band counter the IRQ handler dispatches on: 0, 1, 2, 3, $FF. Each value selects a ULA mode + palette setup. At least four display bands.
16 bytes, written to $FE21 one per entry by irq1v_handler's band 0. The other band computes its palette by stepping the high nibble instead.
the only OS vector Revs claims
mode/pixel rate. Written mid-frame per raster band, from the IRQ handler.
16-entry palette, rewritten per raster band
bit 6 = T1 timeout; the game's interrupt source
free-running timer, READ as a clock/entropy source from six sites across the engine — not a printer port. Needs a real Amiga answer, not a stub.

8x8 shift-add multiply. A = multiplicand (stored to math_lo), $75 = multiplier; 16-bit product in math_lo/math_hi. 27 callers — the single most-called routine in the engine, so the hottest thing to give a 68000 twin.
absolute value of A, 8-bit two's complement (BPL / EOR #$FF / ADC #1). 21 callers.
negate the 16-bit value in math_lo/math_hi if A is negative (i.e. |x| for a sign-magnitude pair). $0E42 is the unconditional-negate entry.
unconditional 16-bit negate of math_lo/math_hi; the fall-through half of abs16_math
low byte of the 16-bit math accumulator (mul8 product, abs16_math operand). $74-$79 are the general scratch/arithmetic window and are reused everywhere.
high byte of the 16-bit math accumulator
